standard.title: Observing and Measuring
standard.description: use equipment to observe, measure and record data with reasonable precision, using digital tools as appropriate
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can read familiar scaled instruments and record observations systematically (AC9S3I03, 3-4 band). They now extend to selecting equipment for precision, using standard units with prefixes, and recording data electronically.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students select equipment appropriate to the precision required, measure and record data using standard units and prefixes, discuss why precision matters for investigation findings, and use digital tools where appropriate.

nodes.label: Equipment is selected for the precision the investigation requires
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can explain why different equipment gives different levels of precision, select appropriate equipment for a given measurement task, and describe the effect of low precision on investigation findings.
nodes.minimum_width: Students compare the precision of two instruments for the same measurement and select the more appropriate one, explaining their reasoning.
nodes.typical_width: Students select appropriate equipment across investigation types, explain why precision matters for investigation conclusions, use standard units with metric prefixes (kilo-, milli-) consistently, and record data in tables, diagrams or digital formats.
wider: Explore which equipment gives the most appropriate precision for different investigation contexts — comparing cup vs measuring jug vs digital scale for mass measurement
Use digital tools (digital photography, spreadsheets) to record and organise observation data — examining what digital recording adds in accuracy and reproducibility
Investigate how the precision of measurement equipment affects whether a difference between two conditions can be detected
nodes.hinge_reason: Precision measurement with appropriate equipment is a prerequisite for I04 data representation and I05 error analysis — students who do not measure with adequate precision cannot construct meaningful representations or identify measurement error as a specific error source. Imprecision at I03 propagates as systematically poor data through all downstream inquiry nodes.

response_modes.reason: Precise measurement with standard units requires consistent accurate practice across investigation types. Students at this band must apply precision reasoning independently — not just follow instructions — which requires encountering precision decisions across varied measurement contexts.

success_criteria: Selects appropriate equipment for a given measurement task and explains the reasoning
Records data using standard units with appropriate metric prefixes
Explains how low precision could affect the conclusions of an investigation
